newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks higher at midday.

text.p: A rally in high techs, driven by strong earnings reports, and a stable albeit lackluster bond market kept Wall Street stocks steady at midday.
The Dow Industrials were up 28 points at 6793 while advances led declining issues by 13 to nine on volume of about 275 million shares.

"First and foremost, you have additional strong earnings in the high technology sector," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Networking stocks continue to do extremely well with Ascend's earnings."
Ascend Communications Inc was up 4-7/8 at 73-3/4 after reporting stronger than anticipated fourth quarter earnings after ethe close of trading on Thursday.

"Ascend did not run-up ahead of the earnings as was the case with some other high technology stocks, like Intel Corp ," Bleier said. "The networking stock have been subject to a lot of questions concerning their earnings and have underperformed the other techs for the last two weeks."
Cisco Systems Inc was up 1-1/2 at 71-7/8 while Cascade Communications Corp was up 3-5/8 at 55-1/2. Intel was up 2-3/8 at 144-3/4.
"I think the market is finally beginning to discount the possibility that corporate growth will be better than had been extended," said Chris Callies of CS First Boston.
U.S. Treasuries have traded both sides of unchanged in a tight range throughout the day and were higher at midday. The long bond was up 5/32 to yield 6.82 percent.

Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at at Amas Securities, said that investors were beginning to focus on special situations concerning individual stocks rather than the movement of the overall averages.
"We are past the point at which the economic recovery affected all industries and there are now a lot of companies which will outstrip the averages," Farley said.
"There will be a gap between the superstars, like Intel or Atmel Corp, and the rest of the market. You cannot continue to have double-digit growth in all companies."
Today's earnings casualties included Uniphase Corp which was down 9-3/8 at 36-1/2 after reporting weaker than forecast second quarter net after the close of trading on Thursday.

Shares of General Motors Corp were down 5/8 at 59-3/4. The company on Thursday announced the sale of Hughes Aircraft to Raytheon Co for $9.5 billion in stock and debt. Raytheon was unchanged at 48-1/2.
Shares of U.S. Robotics were up 2-3/4 at 69-7/8 on America Online Inc's plan to increase spending on network upgrades.
Shares of UAL Corp were down 1-1/4 at 58-3/8 after Salomon Brothers cut its rating on the stock to hold from buy.
